sections.description: Introduces the patient, his presenting symptoms, and the full chronological clinical history leading to the need for a third transcatheter aortic valve intervention. Establishes the broader context of TAVI as an established treatment for aortic stenosis and the emerging clinical challenge of structural valve deterioration requiring repeat interventions in long-term survivors.
subtopics: Patient demographics, presenting symptoms (dyspnea, chest discomfort, dizziness, fatigue), and functional impairment
Comprehensive medical history: three-vessel CAD with multiple PCIs, third-degree AV block with pacemaker, COPD, type 2 diabetes, recurrent GI bleeding
Initial TAVI in 2014 with a 27 mm Lotus valve: indications and clinical context
Progressive structural valve deterioration by 2021–2022: worsening gradients, EF decline, symptom recurrence
First TAV-in-TAV in 2022 with a 23 mm Evolut valve: procedural course, vascular complication, and early hemodynamic improvement
Episode of prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE) in September 2022: Enterococcus faecalis, antimicrobial treatment course, and confirmation of infection resolution
Renewed prosthetic valve dysfunction by January 2024: severe stenosis with moderate-to-severe regurgitation prompting consideration of a third intervention
The growing population of TAVI patients requiring repeat interventions and the concept of lifetime management in structural valve disease

sections.section_title: Pathophysiology of Valve Degeneration and Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis
sections.description: Explains the mechanisms underlying bioprosthetic valve structural deterioration, the pathogenesis and microbiology of prosthetic valve endocarditis, and how these processes converged in this patient to produce severe prosthetic valve dysfunction. Covers the hemodynamic consequences of combined stenosis and regurgitation on left ventricular function.
subtopics: Structural valve deterioration of bioprosthetic transcatheter valves: mechanisms, timing, and contributing factors
Prosthetic valve endocarditis: pathogenesis, risk factors, and Enterococcus faecalis as a causative organism
Interaction between treated endocarditis and structural degeneration in accelerating valve failure: leaflet injury, fibrosis, and mechanical restriction
Hemodynamic consequences of prosthetic valve dysfunction: combined stenosis and regurgitation
The patient's hemodynamic trajectory: EF changes (54% → 42% → 66%) and gradient evolution across interventions
Resolution of PVE and its implications for subsequent procedural decision-making
Why management of prosthetic valve dysfunction after cured endocarditis aligns with standard structural valve deterioration management

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Evaluation and CT-Guided Procedural Planning
sections.description: Details the comprehensive diagnostic workup that established both the severity of prosthetic dysfunction and the absence of active infection, and the advanced CT-based anatomical planning that determined feasibility of a third transcatheter valve. Covers the multidisciplinary risk assessment and decision-making process that led to choosing a transcatheter rather than surgical strategy.
subtopics: Echocardiographic assessment of prosthetic valve dysfunction: TTE and TEE findings, mean gradient, AVA by continuity equation, Doppler velocity index
Confirmation of endocarditis resolution: repeated blood cultures, TEE, and MSCT exclusion of vegetations and paravalvular complications
MSCT for anatomical feasibility assessment: coronary ostial height, sinus of Valsalva dimensions, valve-to-coronary distance
Assessment of frame interaction between Lotus and Evolut prostheses and minimum lumen diameter measurement
Neo-skirt concept: formation mechanism and implications for coronary flow preservation
Coronary obstruction risk stratification and the decision to proceed without coronary protection
Surgical risk assessment: EuroSCORE II of 27.36%, comorbidities, and anatomical complexity of prior valve frames
Multidisciplinary heart team decision-making: interventional cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, imaging specialists, and anesthesiologists
2025 ESC guidelines on PVE management and individualization of treatment strategy

sections.section_title: Procedural Strategy and Technical Execution of TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV
sections.description: Describes the technical aspects of the third transcatheter valve implantation, including the rationale for valve selection, the high-implantation strategy to preserve coronary flow and effective orifice area, commissural alignment considerations, and the step-by-step procedural execution with intra-procedural imaging guidance.
subtopics: Access strategy: left radial and left femoral arterial access under local anesthesia
Acurate neo2 valve selection rationale: supra-annular leaflet positioning, low frame height, favorable hemodynamic performance in narrow anatomies
High implantation strategy at the level of the Evolut valve leaflets: rationale for fixing pre-existing leaflets against the stent frame
Prevention of inward leaflet folding and minimization of neo-skirt formation below coronary ostia
Commissural alignment: CT-guided technique, fluoroscopic landmarks, and importance for future coronary access
Balloon pre-dilation and post-dilation strategy: balloon sizing, rapid ventricular pacing, and potential contribution to Evolut frame expansion
Intra-procedural aortography: confirmation of coronary flow, valve positioning, and absence of regurgitation
Step-by-step procedural sequence from guidewire placement to final aortographic assessment
Institutional approval for off-label use and shared decision-making with the patient and family

sections.description: Covers the post-procedural course including early hemodynamic results, the phenomenon of patient-prosthesis mismatch and its resolution over time, and the 1-year clinical and echocardiographic follow-up. Distills the key clinical lessons regarding lifetime management of patients with serial transcatheter valve interventions and future therapeutic options.
subtopics: Immediate post-procedural assessment according to VARC-3 criteria: valve deployment, regurgitation grade, and complication evaluation
Early post-implantation hemodynamics: elevated mean gradient (67 mm Hg), reduced AVA (0.9 cm²), and severe patient-prosthesis mismatch
Hemodynamic evolution at 1 month: gradient reduction to 27 mm Hg, AVA increase to 1.1 cm², and LV remodeling
Mechanisms of gradient resolution: commissural alignment, post-dilation effects, and partial mechanical expansion of the prior Evolut frame
Patient-prosthesis mismatch: definition, clinical significance, and recognition in the transcatheter context
3.5-month and 1-year follow-up: clinical stability, exercise tolerance, preserved valve function, and absence of recurrent endocarditis
Challenges of future interventions in triple-stented anatomy: coronary access, surgical explantation risk, and limited remaining options
Emerging catheter-based solutions: BASILICA and bioprosthetic valve fracture—potential and uncertainties in triple-valve configurations
Principles of lifetime management planning: importance of forward-looking strategy from the first TAVI, frame layering, and long-term surveillance
